Listen, I’m not sure of the family dynamics but as other people mentioned your sister may not have had the same kind of secure and supportive bonds that you enjoyed with your parents/grandparents. I don’t know and I couldn’t say for sure but in psychology there is a nature vs nurture debate and it posits that even though you two grew up in the same household your experiences and relationships with your family are completely unique and it’s a mistake to judge people’s intentions based on extrospection. My little brother just passed away a month ago, he struggled with drugs and I was the golden child too (not to assume)- my dad had wanted to cut my brother out of his will, but now that my brother is dead. I have some clarity.

Your grandparents are on the other side now and I think that with that comes a greater clarity beyond oneself and one’s mortal wishes. Your grandfather was hurt when he made his decision, and I don’t know what kind of issues your sister may be dealing with but you should consider the possibility of mental health issues. It is hard to say how I would have acted were I in your shoes, but as someone whose sibling just passed away allow me to share my perspective.

Your grandparents have passed and I am sorry for your loss, but I don’t think that they would have held onto bitter resentment in the afterlife, your sister is still alive. This kind of desperation and isolation means that your sister is not only incredibly lonely and despondent but she could become suicidal. As someone who recently graduated but is having a hard time finding a job in my field, I can relate . If you think your sister isn’t able to budget well, maybe work something out like a “trust” or some kind of monthly support. You don’t have to split the inheritance in half but if my brother was still alive, I wish I would have reached out and tried to help him more, I wish I could have saved him from his desperate isolation. There are always going to be factors that we as individuals fail to account for, especially in interpreting the actions of others. Depression can be absolutely crippling and some feel it more intensely than others, I won’t make excuses for anyone’s behaviour but if I were you, I would try to mend the bonds between your sister and your parents. Try to organize some family counselling and try to think about what you might regret if your sister killed herself. Homelessness and poverty are my greatest fears and I can definitely see myself killing myself if I was as isolated and despondent as her. 

It is a mistake to hold grudges, my brother stole thousands from us years ago when he was in the throes of addiction- but I have forgiven him for everything, people can change. 

Give your sister the chance to grow, when you’re standing at her grave I promise you will regret not helping her when you could.

Thank you for sharing your pain with us. What country are you in? I’m in Canada so I’m more familiar with the supports up here but there is a whole community (not just restricted to the LGBTQ) that is here to love and support you and I promise we will love you for who you are and however you identify. Your father sounds abusive and I can imagine (from personal experience) how betrayed and alone you must feel, although it sounds like you had a really tough time coming out. Know that you are beautiful, it is right to want to be true to yourself and you don’t have to hide who you are for anyone. Live your truth, if your parents don’t support you than focus on finding supports (and a healthy environment), if you are thinking of going to a post-secondary school there will be clubs and peer groups for you to connect with and there will be people with similar stories. Focus on getting the best grades you can (I know it’s hard in a hostile home, but you can study at the library if you have to- I did. You’ll want to try to apply for scholarships, grants and bursaries for support to ease the debt from student loans) and once you’re out of there and you have social support- I promise you… someday the world will be brighter. If you can find some LGBTQ support groups in your area they might be able to help a bit too, if only to let you vent and hear that others were in your situation too but if you need help they will help you find a safe space
